stem_html:
The choreographer's instructions to the dancers are deliberately ______: she names a quality the movement should have and refuses to say which joint should produce it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "underspecified"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "contradictory", "trap": "too-extreme"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "severe", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "improvised", "trap": "half-right"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The colon says what she does and what she declines to do.
  • Incomplete is not the same as inconsistent.
  • Ask whose behaviour the blank describes.

Why A is right She supplies one thing and withholds another: she “names a quality the movement should have and refuses to say which joint” delivers it. An instruction that leaves the means open is underspecified.

Why B is wrong Contradictory would require two instructions that cannot both be followed. She gives one, incompletely.

Why C is wrong Severe is about the tone of the instruction, and the colon describes its content.

Why D is wrong The improvising is the dancers'; the instruction itself is written and deliberate.

stem_html:
The two accounts of the strike are not opposed so much as ______: the union's records begin on the morning the mill closed, and the owner's end the night before.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "complementary"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "identical", "trap": "too-extreme"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "unreliable", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "competing", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • “Not X so much as Y” needs Y to differ from X.
  • Adjoining is neither overlapping nor conflicting.
  • One choice restates the word the sentence rejects.

Why A is right One record stops where the other starts — “the union's records begin on the morning the mill closed, and the owner's end the night before” — so together they cover the whole and neither overlaps the other. That is complementarity.

Why B is wrong Identical accounts would cover the same ground, and these cover adjoining ground.

Why C is wrong Nothing questions the accuracy of either record; the colon describes their coverage.

Why D is wrong Competing is a near-synonym for opposed, which the sentence has just ruled out.

stem_html:
The reforms proved ______ in a way their authors had not intended: each measure worked as designed, and the four of them together produced a delay longer than the one they were meant to remove.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "self-defeating"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "ineffective", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "unpopular", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "ambitious", "trap": "out-of-scope"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Every part succeeding and the whole failing is the shape.
  • Failing to work and working against yourself are different.
  • The blank must describe the outcome.

Why A is right Every measure worked and the aggregate reversed the goal, so the reforms defeated themselves by succeeding. That is what “each measure worked as designed” makes precise.

Why B is wrong Ineffective would mean the measures did not work, and the sentence says each one did.

Why C is wrong Public reaction is never mentioned.

Why D is wrong Ambition describes the aim rather than the outcome the sentence reports.

stem_html:
The following text is adapted from a 2017 article about weather records.

The longest continuous rainfall record in the country was kept not by a government office but by four generations of one family, who measured the gauge in their yard at seven each morning for a hundred and twelve years. Meteorologists were slow to use it, since it had no official standing. They use it now for the reason they once ignored it: nobody changed the instrument, the site, or the hour.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "To explain how the feature that once disqualified a record turned out to be what made it valuable."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "To criticize meteorologists for neglecting amateur observations.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "To describe the daily routine that produced a long rainfall record.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "To argue that official weather stations should be run by families.", "trap": "too-extreme"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Purpose is the turn, not the topic.
  • The final sentence names the reversal outright.
  • Reported delay is not stated criticism.

Why A is right The last sentence turns the objection into the reason: they use it now “for the reason they once ignored it”, which is the unbroken method.

Why B is wrong The delay is reported without blame, and criticism is not the point the text builds to.

Why C is wrong The routine is the evidence for the reversal rather than the purpose.

Why D is wrong No such recommendation appears.

stem_html:
The following text is adapted from a 2016 essay on museum lighting.

Curators speak of light as a debt. A watercolour can be shown for so many hours in its life and no more, and every exhibition draws on an account that is never replenished. The question is therefore not whether to darken a gallery but whom to darken it for, since the visitor kept in the dark today is the reason a visitor in 2200 will see anything at all.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "It converts the technical constraint described earlier into a question about competing audiences, which the rest of the sentence answers."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "It concedes that darkening galleries is unpopular with visitors.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "It introduces a second constraint that the text goes on to weigh against the first.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "It restates the metaphor of the debt in nontechnical language.", "trap": "half-right"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Ask what changes between the sentence before and the sentence after.
  • “Not whether but whom” is a reframing.
  • Restating and reframing are different jobs.

Why A is right The preceding sentences set up a fixed budget of hours; the underlined clause makes it a choice — “not whether to darken a gallery but whom to darken it for” — between today's visitor and a visitor in 2200, which the closing clause then settles.

Why B is wrong Popularity is never raised.

Why C is wrong No second constraint appears; the same one is restated as a choice.

Why D is wrong It does more than restate: it changes the subject of the question from whether to whom.

stem_html:
Text 1

Requiring code to be published alongside a paper has raised the quality of computational research. Since the policy took effect, the proportion of results in this journal that an independent group can reproduce has risen from about a third to nearly three-quarters.

Text 2

The rise is real, but the policy did not cause all of it. Groups that were unable or unwilling to release code stopped submitting here, and their papers now appear elsewhere. A journal that has changed which studies it receives cannot read its own reproducibility rate as a measure of how much research improved.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely characterize the increase reported in Text 1?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "As partly an effect of a change in which studies the journal receives rather than of better practice alone."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "As a fabrication produced by selective reporting of reproducibility tests.", "trap": "too-extreme"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "As proof that mandatory code release should be adopted by every journal.", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "As too small to establish that the policy had any effect.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Selection effects concede the number and dispute the cause.
  • “The rise is real” rules out the fraud reading.
  • Partly is the word to look for.

Why A is right Text 2 grants the rise and reassigns part of it: “groups that were unable or unwilling to release code stopped submitting here”, so the pool changed as well as the practice.

Why B is wrong Text 2 opens by saying the rise is real, so it charges no fabrication.

Why C is wrong That is Text 1's conclusion, not Text 2's.

Why D is wrong Text 2 never disputes the size of the increase, only what it measures.

stem_html: An economist argued that a city's new bus lane reduced car journey times on parallel streets because it removed buses from the general traffic, not because it reduced the total number of cars. Which finding, if true, would most directly support the economist's argument?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Car counts on the parallel streets were unchanged after the lane opened, while the number of times a car had to stop behind a bus fell by four-fifths."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Average car journey times on the parallel streets fell by three minutes after the lane opened.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "Bus ridership rose by 12 percent in the year after the lane opened.", "trap": "true-but-irrelevant"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "Car counts on the parallel streets fell by a fifth after the lane opened.", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • “Because X, not because Y” needs Y held constant.
  • Confirming the effect is not identifying the cause.
  • The rejected mechanism is always offered as a choice.

Why A is right The argument is that the lane worked “because it removed buses from the general traffic, not because it reduced the total number of cars”, so the finding has to hold car numbers steady while the bus interaction changes. Unchanged counts with stops behind buses down four-fifths does exactly that.

Why B is wrong This confirms the effect and says nothing about which mechanism produced it.

Why C is wrong Ridership is about buses, and the claim is about what happened to cars.

Why D is wrong Fewer cars is the rival explanation the economist rejects.

stem_html: A paleontologist claimed that a set of fossil trackways was made by a single animal walking in a circle rather than by several animals walking in a line. Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the claim?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Every print in the sequence shows the same healed fracture in the third toe, and the depth of the prints changes gradually and continuously around the circle."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "The prints are all the same size and shape.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "The trackway forms a closed loop about nine metres across.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "No other trackways of the same age occur at the site.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Look for the feature that is individual, not typical.
  • A pathology is a signature; a shape is not.
  • Both hypotheses predict a loop.

Why A is right The claim is that the trackways were made “by a single animal walking in a circle rather than by several animals”, and a healed fracture is individual, so a print carrying it at every step must come from one animal. Continuously changing depth rules out separate animals arriving at intervals.

Why B is wrong Animals of one species leave prints of the same size and shape, so this fits both explanations.

Why C is wrong A line of animals following one another can also trace a loop.

Why D is wrong The absence of other trackways says nothing about how this one was made.

stem_html:
Researchers measured how accurately listeners identified the emotion in short speech clips played in four conditions. They concluded that removing the words while keeping the melody of the voice cost listeners very little, whereas removing the melody while keeping the words cost them a great deal.

Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researchers' conclusion?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Accuracy fell from 84% with full speech to 79% when only the melody remained, but to 46% when only the words remained."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Accuracy was highest with full speech and lowest when neither cue remained.", "trap": "true-but-irrelevant"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "Accuracy with only the words remaining was 46%, well above the 27% obtained when neither cue remained.", "trap": "wrong-part-of-passage"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "Accuracy with only the melody remaining was 79%, the second-highest value in the graph.", "trap": "half-right"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Two losses means two subtractions from one baseline.
  • Comparing to the floor answers a different question.
  • A rank is not a magnitude.

Why A is right The conclusion is that “removing the words while keeping the melody of the voice cost listeners very little” while the reverse cost a great deal, so it compares two losses against the same baseline. Only this choice gives both: 5 points lost when the words go, 38 when the melody goes.

Why B is wrong The two extremes are consistent with any ordering of the middle two conditions.

Why C is wrong This compares the words condition with the floor rather than with full speech.

Why D is wrong One value with a rank is not a comparison of the two losses.

stem_html: In his memoir Downriver, Teodoro Vasquez describes his father's silence not as an absence of speech but as a form of instruction the son only recognized years later. Which quotation from a fictional memoir would best illustrate this claim?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "“He would not name the tree for me. He stood there until I had walked round it twice, and it is thirty years before I understood that this was the lesson and not the withholding of one.”"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "“My father rarely spoke, and when he did it was about the weather or the engine.”", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "“He taught me the names of every tree on the river, patiently, one afternoon at a time.”", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "“His silence hurt me then and it hurts me now, and I have never found the use in it.”", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • The claim has two halves: instruction, and delayed recognition.
  • A quotation that reports the silence without meaning fails the first half.
  • Explicit denial of the claim is a common distractor.

Why A is right The claim is that the silence was “a form of instruction the son only recognized years later”. Here it is deliberate and pedagogical — he waits while the son circles the tree — and the recognition is explicitly delayed by thirty years.

Why B is wrong This reports the silence as a habit and finds no instruction in it.

Why C is wrong Here the father teaches by speaking, which is the opposite of the claim.

Why D is wrong This narrator explicitly denies ever finding a use in the silence.

stem_html:
The following text is adapted from a 2022 article about seed banks.

A seed bank stores what a crop is at the moment of storage. A field, by contrast, stores what a crop is becoming: the varieties farmers keep planting change every season in response to the pests and weather of that season. A bank protects a variety from extinction and, at the same time, stops it adapting. Both kinds of conservation are necessary, and neither can substitute for the other.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Storing seed and continuing to grow a crop preserve different things, so both are needed."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Seed banks are the most reliable way of protecting crop varieties from extinction.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "Farmers change the varieties they plant in response to pests and weather.", "trap": "wrong-part-of-passage"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "Crops kept in seed banks eventually lose the ability to adapt to new conditions.", "trap": "too-extreme"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • A both/neither sentence is usually the main idea.
  • A contrast asks for an answer that keeps both sides.
  • Halting adaptation is not destroying the capacity for it.

Why A is right The passage contrasts the two and closes on the claim that “both kinds of conservation are necessary, and neither can substitute for the other”.

Why B is wrong Reliability is not compared, and the text's point is that banking alone is not enough.

Why C is wrong This is a supporting detail about fields.

Why D is wrong The text says a bank stops a variety adapting while stored, not that the variety loses a capacity.

stem_html:
The following text is adapted from a 2015 essay on maps.

The surveyors who made the first accurate map of the delta worked for eleven years and produced a document that was obsolete on the day it was printed. Channels there move faster than surveyors can walk. What the map preserved was not the delta but the surveyors' route through it, and that route is now the only record of villages the river has since taken.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "A map that failed at its intended purpose became valuable as a record of something else."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Surveying a delta accurately is impossible because its channels move.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "The surveyors spent eleven years on a document that was never used.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "Rivers destroy villages faster than mapmakers can record them.", "trap": "wrong-part-of-passage"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Failure plus unexpected value is the shape.
  • The setup is not the point.
  • The last sentence carries the second value.

Why A is right The map is obsolete as a map, and the closing sentence gives it a second value: the route is “the only record of villages the river has since taken”.

Why B is wrong The difficulty is the setup, not the point the text arrives at.

Why C is wrong The text says the opposite of never used — the record is used now.

Why D is wrong This turns a detail about the villages into the main claim.

stem_html:
Two identical batches of a fermented sauce were left in cellars of the same temperature and humidity, one in a building of stone and one of timber. After nine months the timber-cellar batch carried three yeast species absent from the stone batch, and those three were the species found on the timber itself. Since the ingredients and the conditions were the same, the difference in the finished sauce ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "is most plausibly explained by organisms the building itself contributed."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "shows that timber cellars produce better sauce than stone ones.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "indicates that the two batches were not in fact identical at the start.", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "means temperature has no effect on fermentation.", "trap": "too-extreme"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • What varied is the only candidate cause.
  • The matching species name the source.
  • A held-constant variable is untested, not disproved.

Why A is right The controlled variables cannot explain a difference, and the three extra species “were the species found on the timber itself”, which points at the building as the source.

Why B is wrong Quality is never assessed; only composition differs.

Why C is wrong The passage states the batches were identical, so this contradicts the premise rather than following from it.

Why D is wrong Holding temperature constant shows nothing about what temperature does.

stem_html:
A publisher offered readers a choice between a printed newsletter and an email version. Subscriptions to the printed version fell by half over three years while total subscriptions rose by a fifth, and surveys found that readers who switched cited delivery speed rather than cost, which was the same for both. This suggests that the decline in printed subscriptions ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "reflects readers moving between formats rather than losing interest in the newsletter."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "was caused by the higher price of the printed version.", "trap": "reversed-relationship"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "will continue until the printed version is discontinued.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "shows that readers prefer shorter newsletters.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • A falling part inside a rising whole is a shift.
  • Check the choice against the stated reason.
  • An inference is not a forecast.

Why A is right Total subscriptions rose while print fell, so readers stayed with the publication and changed format — and they “cited delivery speed rather than cost” for doing so.

Why B is wrong The passage says cost “was the same for both”.

Why C is wrong A prediction requires evidence about the future that the passage does not give.

Why D is wrong Length is never mentioned; the two versions carry the same newsletter.

The bridge was designed to carry a tram that was never built ______ its deck is twice as wide as the traffic it now takes requires.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "; as a result,"}, {"letter": "B", "content": ", as a result,", "trap": "comma-splice-plausible"}, {"letter": "C", "content": " as a result,", "trap": "comma-splice-plausible"}, {"letter": "D", "content": ", as a result", "trap": "comma-splice-plausible"}]

stem_html:
The lens that the observatory ground in 1897 ______ still the largest refracting lens ever put into regular service, weighs half a tonne.

Why D is wrong In addition adds the second event to the first, but the second replaces the first.

Two independent laboratories reported the same anomalous decay rate, using different detectors and different samples. ______ the result cannot be dismissed as an artifact of one instrument.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Accordingly,"}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Nevertheless,", "trap": "transition-reversal"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "For example,", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "By contrast,", "trap": "transition-reversal"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Evidence then conclusion is a consequence.
  • Two detectors is the reason, so the transition is causal.
  • Contrast words need two sides that disagree.

Why A is right The second sentence is the conclusion the first supports: independent replication is precisely what rules out a single-instrument artifact.

Why B is wrong Nevertheless marks a contrast, and the two sentences agree.

Why C is wrong The second sentence is an inference, not an instance of the first.

Why D is wrong There is no contrast between the evidence and the conclusion drawn from it.

stem_html:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Composer Florence Price finished her Symphony in E minor in 1932.
  • It was premiered by the Chicago Symphony Orchestra in 1933.
  • She was the first Black woman whose symphony was played by a major American orchestra.
  • The score was lost for decades and was found in an abandoned house in 2009.

The student wants to emphasize the precariousness of Price's legacy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices_json: [{"letter": "A", "content": "Although Price's symphony made her the first Black woman played by a major American orchestra, the score was lost for decades and recovered only in 2009, from an abandoned house."}, {"letter": "B", "content": "Florence Price finished her Symphony in E minor in 1932, and the Chicago Symphony Orchestra premiered it in 1933.", "trap": "out-of-scope"}, {"letter": "C", "content": "Price was the first Black woman whose symphony was performed by a major American orchestra.", "trap": "half-right"}, {"letter": "D", "content": "The score of Price's symphony was found in an abandoned house in 2009.", "trap": "half-right"}]
explanation_html:
Traps in this question

  • Precariousness is a relation between value and risk.
  • One note cannot show a relation between two.
  • Although is the join that carries it.

Why A is right Precariousness needs the achievement and the near-loss in one sentence, and only this choice sets the milestone against decades of the score being missing.

Why B is wrong Two dates, with nothing at risk in either.

Why C is wrong The achievement alone, which is the secure half.

Why D is wrong The loss alone, with nothing to say what was nearly lost.
